'''Douglas Charles "Doug" Rees''' (born 1952) is an American biochemist, biophysicist, and structural biologist.<ref name=epmc>{{EuropePMC|ORCID=0000-0003-4073-1185}}</ref>

==Academic career==
Rees graduated from [[Yale University]] with a bachelor's degree in 1974 working with [[Carolyn Slayman]] and received a PhD in biophysics from [[Harvard University]] in 1980.<ref name='vf'>{{cite web |title=Douglas C Rees, PhD |url=https://thevalleefoundation.org/programs/vvp/douglas-c-rees-phd |website=The Vallee Foundation |access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Kalte |first1=Pamela |last2=Nemeh |first2=Katherine |title=American men & women of science: a biographical directory of today's leaders in physical, biological and related sciences |date=2004 |publisher=Gale Group |location=Detroit |isbn=0787665231 |edition=21.}}</ref> He subsequently completed a postdoctoral fellowshing with James B. Howard at the [[University of Minnesota]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Hageman Distinguished Lecturer in Agricultural Biochemistry |url=https://www.k-state.edu/bmb/about/seminars/hageman/2016-Rees.html |website=Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biophysics |publisher=Kansas State University |access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref>. In 1982 he went to the [[University of California, Los Angeles]].<ref name='vf' /> In 1989, he became a professor of chemistry at [[Caltech]].<ref name='vf' /> There he is Roscoe Gilkey Dickinson Professor and was Dean of graduate studies from 2015-2020.<ref name='caltech'>{{cite web |title=Douglas C. (Doug) Rees |url=https://cce.caltech.edu/people/douglas-c-doug-rees |publisher=Caltech |access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref> From 1997 to 2025, he was an investigator of the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Douglas C. Rees, PhD |url=https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/douglas-c-rees |website=HHMI |publisher=Howard Hughes Medical Institute |access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref>. He served as the [[editor-in-chief|editor]] or co-editor of the ''[[Annual Review of Biophysics and Biomolecular Structure]]'' (2004&ndash;2014).<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1146/annurev.bb.33.051304.100011|title=Preface by Douglas C. Rees|year=2004|last1=Rees|first1=Douglas C.|journal=Annual Review of Biophysics and Biomolecular Structure|volume=33}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1146/annurev-bb-41-050712-100001|title=Preface|year=2012|last1=Rees|first1=Douglas C.|journal=Annual Review of Biophysics|volume=41}}</ref>

==Scientific interests==
He examines the structure and function of metal-containing and membrane proteins,<ref name='caltech' /> especially [[nitrogenase]] in biological nitrogen fixation,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Howard |first1=James B. |last2=Rees |first2=Douglas C. |title=Structural Basis of Biological Nitrogen Fixation |journal=Chemical Reviews |date=1 January 1996 |volume=96 |issue=7 |pages=2965–2982 |doi=10.1021/cr9500545}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Einsle |first1=Oliver |last2=Tezcan |first2=F. Akif |last3=Andrade |first3=Susana L. A. |last4=Schmid |first4=Benedikt |last5=Yoshida |first5=Mika |last6=Howard |first6=James B. |last7=Rees |first7=Douglas C. |title=Nitrogenase MoFe-Protein at 1.16 Å Resolution: A Central Ligand in the FeMo-Cofactor |journal=Science |date=6 September 2002 |volume=297 |issue=5587 |pages=1696–1700 |doi=10.1126/science.1073877}}</ref> and membrane proteins including [[ABC transporters]] and [[Mechanosensitive channels|mechanosensitive ion channels]] including [[Large-conductance mechanosensitive channel|MscL]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chang |first1=Geoffrey |last2=Spencer |first2=Robert H. |last3=Lee |first3=Allen T. |last4=Barclay |first4=Margaret T. |last5=Rees |first5=Douglas C. |title=Structure of the MscL Homolog from Mycobacterium tuberculosis : A Gated Mechanosensitive Ion Channel |journal=Science |date=18 December 1998 |volume=282 |issue=5397 |pages=2220–2226 |doi=10.1126/science.282.5397.2220}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Liu |first1=Zhenfeng |last2=Gandhi |first2=Chris S. |last3=Rees |first3=Douglas C. |title=Structure of a tetrameric MscL in an expanded intermediate state |journal=Nature |date=September 2009 |volume=461 |issue=7260 |pages=120–124 |doi=10.1038/nature08277|pmc=2737600 }}</ref> and [[Small-conductance mechanosensitive channel|MscS]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bass |first1=Randal B. |last2=Strop |first2=Pavel |last3=Barclay |first3=Margaret |last4=Rees |first4=Douglas C. |title=Crystal Structure of Escherichia coli MscS, a Voltage-Modulated and Mechanosensitive Channel |journal=Science |date=22 November 2002 |volume=298 |issue=5598 |pages=1582–1587 |doi=10.1126/science.1077945}}</ref>. To do this, his group uses [[X-ray crystallography]]. His interest in nitrogenase began in [[William Lipscomb]]'s laboratory.{{Citation needed|reason=this needs a source|date=April 2026}}

==Recognition==
In 2015 he received the [[F. Albert Cotton|FA Cotton Medal]]<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wang |first1=Linda |title=Cotton Medal To Douglas Rees |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/93/i10/Cotton-Medal-Douglas-Rees.html |access-date=14 April 2026 |publisher=C&EN |date=9 March 2015}}</ref>, and in 2020 he was awarded the [[Gregori Aminoff Prize]]<ref>{{cite news |title=Studies of enzyme systems rewarded with the Aminoff Prize |url=https://www.iucr.org/news/newsletter/volume-27/number-4/studies-of-enzyme-systems-rewarded-with-the-aminoff-prize |access-date=14 April 2026 |work=IUCr Newsletter |volume=27 |issue=4 |publisher=IUCr |date=18 December 2019}}</ref>. He is a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Douglas C. Rees |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/douglas-c-rees |website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences |publisher=AAAS |access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref>, [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Douglas C. Rees |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/douglas-c-rees-x0j4gc/ |website=National Academy of Sciences |publisher=NAS |access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref>, and was a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Research Fellow]]{{Citation needed|reason=this needs a source|date=April 2026}}.

==Personal==
Rees grew up in [[Lexington, Kentucky]] where his father was a faculty member in the [[University of Kentucky College of Medicine]]<ref>{{cite web |title=William N. Lipscomb Centennial Celebration |url=https://xray.uky.edu/News/Lipscomb.html |website=William N. Lipscomb Centennial Celebration |publisher=University of Kentucky |access-date=14 April 2026}}</ref>
